purpose: A relationship target must be spelled the way the lane spells its own symbols. Every other gate in the family asks whether an edge that EXISTS is right; none asked whether the target is a NAME at all, and the differential oracle cannot ask it because its truth comes from the same rules the analyzer runs — when both sides fabricate the same spelling, they agree. The first measurement found whole expression surfaces published as targets (source text with comments, lambdas, test-description strings, generic type expressions, `$`-sigil values) in 12 of 24 lanes, all of it invisible to the differential by construction.

convicting.literal: the WHOLE target is a quoted string or a bare number — no language in the family declares such a symbol; needs no calibration and cannot false-positive
convicting.whitespace: the target contains a space, tab or newline. CONVICTING, but SPLIT BY OWNER before it is acted on, because the rationale this class was first convicted on ('no identifier in any of these languages may contain whitespace') is REFUTED by the artifact — the same way the first draft of `separator` was refuted, and the retraction is recorded rather than quietly dropped. Measured (script/m14/tmp/r10-whitespace-split-probe.ts, on the real corpus files the artifact names): scala and groovy DO declare identifiers containing whitespace (scala's `` `popAll preserves iteration order` `` and groovy's `test entity with trait property` are quoted method names) and their lanes publish the very same string as a SYMBOL name, so the target is honest. `whitespaceSubclasses` on every lane pins the split exactly, and each subclass routes: `operatorMember` (the whole last dotted segment is `operator` + whitespace + a token) is the C2b member-NAMING question and not a spelling one — csharp's `operator ==` is its own symbol's name and the containment edge agrees; `payloadSigil` (the target begins with `@`) is a decorator/annotation payload or a sigil-quoted identifier published as if it were a name; `matchesOwnSymbol` means the lane is SELF-CONSISTENT — the string is one of the names that lane itself publishes, so no per-edge gate can adjudicate it (this holds for the honest quoted names AND for the lanes whose published name carries the quoting syntax, kotlin's `` `test char column read and write` `` and zig's `@"zls env"`, AND for a lane that publishes an EXPRESSION as a name, haskell's `M1 i c` and scala's `A, B` — three different owners, which is why it is routed and not excused); `sourceText` (the string is not a name the lane declares at all — a comment, a call expression, a type expression) is the only subclass R10 itself owns. Every subclass count is compared EXACTLY by the gate, so a target cannot be reclassified without re-running this writer. The routed halves are cited where they are owned: every lane whose split carries `matchesOwnSymbol` or `payloadSigil` counts now cites #924 (`M60 name surface`), and #924's definition of done requires exactly that citation, so a routed conviction is a handoff rather than an excuse.
convicting.delimiter: the target contains `;`, `(`, `)`, `{`, `}` or `,` — statement and grouping syntax, never part of a name
convicting.whitespaceRuled_operatorMember: RULED 2026-09-23 (owner decision, C2b): a whitespace-bearing OPERATOR MEMBER name (`operator ==`, `operator ?`, `operator <`, `operator()`, `implicit Box<Plain>`) is a NAMING CONVENTION of the lane's contract, not a fabrication, so it is measured and pinned but NOT convicted. The ruling is evidence-backed: (1) it is exactly what the declaration writes — the grammar spells an operator declaration `operator` + whitespace + the token, and the lane's containment edge agrees; (2) the lane already publishes a whitespace-bearing operator name BY DESIGN — csharp's conversion operators are `implicit Box<Plain>` (pinned in qualified-type-spelling.expectation.json, `implicit int` in payload-and-complexity) and using-alias-and-operators.expectation.json states in its own rationale that 'every ordinary operator keeps its exact pre-R1 spelling (`operator +`, `operator checked +`, `operator ==`, `implicit int`), because the whole lane's expectations name these symbols' — convicting one half of the convention would contradict the half that is pinned and mutated; (3) 'referenceable' was never the test — no source in these languages references an operator member by name (operators are invoked, `a == b`, never named), so it does not distinguish a convention from a fabrication here. The ruled counts remain pinned in `whitespaceRuled` and inside `whitespaceSubclasses`, so a lane emitting a new operator-member shape fails the gate until the register is rewritten, and every ruled sub-class must carry a WRITTEN REASON in `subclassRulings` — an unreasoned ruling fails exactly as an unruled separator triple does. java.note: PAID DOWN 2026-09-23, measured (R10 sibling sweep). The conviction was a DERIVATION defect, not a target-shape one, and it is why this lane's 3 rows looked like two different classes. An override endpoint is `${ownerFqn}.${name}${signature}`, so the label came from splitting a string that CONTAINS a parameter list, and the pre-fix rule (split on '.', keep the last two segments, cut each at '(') split the parameter list itself whenever a parameter TYPE was written with a dot: `handle.Criterion,StringBuilder,StringBuilder,String,int,List,ConversionService,boolean,boolean)` on both ends (grails-core JpaQueryBuilder.java:271, the anonymous QueryHandler) and `removeEldestEntry.Entry<String, Boolean>)` (GrailsResourceUtils.java:196/:203, the anonymous LinkedHashMap), where the honest keys are `anonymous_QueryHandler.handle` and `LinkedHashMap.removeEldestEntry`. LIVE IN THE DIFFERENTIAL, measured same-files rather than argued: at 300 files of grails-core the PRE-fix tree (bdce721a, hash 320384d592ae9cbb, 4,600 analyzer edges, 4,036 truth edges, heuristic 581) read MISSING=1 / unexplained=1, and the two rows were the same defect — `MISSING overrides anonymous_QueryHandler.handle -> QueryHandler.handle` and `UNEXPLAINED overrides handle.Criterion,…,boolean) -> handle.Criterion,…,boolean) (line 271)`; POST-fix on the identical file set the rows are MISSING=0 / unexplained=0 with every other number unchanged. The canonical 60-file draw never sampled that file, which is why the lane was green. FIX: one shared rule, `localEdgeLabel` in src/ast/override-context.ts (delete every balanced parenthesised group, then split on dots and keep the last two segments), now called by java, groovy AND csharp. The sibling half is measured, not assumed: groovy and csharp wore the MIRROR of the same class (`split('(')[0]` first — immune to the parameter-list split, but it truncates a paren-bearing OWNER chain to a wrong-but-name-shaped label, `Child.getInner().anonymous_Inner.foo` -> `Child.getInner`), and on the same-file-set draws their relabel moved NOTHING (grails-core groovy hash b1d93874cfcbfdee, powershell csharp hash d29d60a18c797e0f, both byte-identical before and after), which is the honest form of 'latent here, closed by construction'. PROOFS: script/m60/edge-label-rule-probe.ts (18-row shape table; negative proof — the superseded rules are wrong on 8/18 and 5/18 rows, so the table can fail), validation/m14/fixtures/java/override-key-parameter-lists.* plus the csharp and groovy siblings, and mutant `java/override-label-parameter-list` (CAUGHT, its new failure being the java fixture). rust.note: CONVICTED AND PAID DOWN 2026-09-24 (rust #798, R10). This lane's `convictions` map was EMPTY, and its artifact row read `clean`, while the lane was in fact publishing source text as a target — the empty map was a statement about the DRAW, not about the lane. Measured: `bun script/m60/target-spelling-census.ts --lane rust --sample 667` on the pre-fix analyzer reported `anomalies=6 {"whitespace":6}`, all `references` targets, subclass `matchesOwnSymbol` — 5x `references -> "&mut ProcessBuilder"` and 1x `references -> "&mut Execs"`, every one of them at cargo/crates/cargo-test-support/src/lib.rs. THE DRAW BLIND SPOT, MEASURED AND FILED: the census's canonical draw is 40 files per corpus (sorted, every k-th), and the violating file is ABSENT from cargo's draw at caps 40, 60, 240 and 700 while it is drawn at 400 and 1400 (script/m14/tmp/rust-798-draw-check.ts). At the canonical cap 40 this lane would therefore have read `clean` forever, and the register's `clean` was true about the sample and false about the lane. The class is one ROOT with three surfaces, and the census only measures one of them: `impl ChannelChangerCommandExt for &mut ProcessBuilder` published the impl SYMBOL under the name `&mut ProcessBuilder`, the same text as the `implements` edge's SOURCE and as each member's OWNER, and `Self` resolution inside the block made it a `references` TARGET (5 rows, plus `&mut Execs` x1). THE FIX (R10, this round): the implemented type's NOMINAL name is published — a reference/pointer/parenthesized wrapper is transparent, so `&mut ProcessBuilder` IS `ProcessBuilder`; a type with NO nominal name (a slice `[u8]`, a tuple `(T, U)`) takes the family's declared synthetic `anonymous_impl` on the impl SYMBOL with the source spelling kept in `metadata.implementedType`, while `Self` resolution takes ABSENCE (R7: the honest state is absence, not a placeholder, and the synthetic block name is never substituted for the type in a TARGET position). RE-MEASURED at full extent, not on a draw: `--lane rust --sample 2285` (ripgrep 110 + cargo 1241 files, 182,977 relationships) reads `clean` with `anomalies=0 sep=0 unruled=-`, and the F5 differential at the same files reports 0 missing / 0 unexplained against its independently-written oracle (6,309 and 41,793 truth edges). TWO ADJACENT FINDINGS this work surfaced, recorded here because they belong to the same root: (1) `calls -> "Self"` — the KEYWORD published as a callee name, 6 rows on cargo (`Ok(Self(name))` in cargo-util-schemas/src/manifest/mod.rs, `Self(ProcessEnv)` in build-rs/src/input.rs). Found by the F14 name-surface gate when it was extended to rust (this census cannot see it: `Self` is a well-SPELLED name, and R10's classes are about spelling); the callee now resolves to the enclosing impl type, exactly as `Name(..)` does, and a trait default body (no impl to resolve) omits the edge. (2) RAW IDENTIFIERS keep their `r#` prefix on the symbol AND everything that targets it (`r#try`, `r#async`) and are DECLARED by the F14 gate as the identifier's own spelling rather than tolerated: the prefix is the only way the identifier can be written in source, both sides carry it (so it resolves), and R2 of the gate REFUSES the stripped form by name, since `try`/`async` are keywords. Measured: ripgrep 1 symbol + 1 target, cargo 2 symbols + 11 targets.

go.note: SPLIT AND MEASURED (#799 round, R10). Two mechanisms shared these triples at the start of the round, and only one of them was a convention. (1) The QUALIFIED TYPE USE was NOT a convention: `references/declared_type` and `references/return_type` published the USE spelling (`io.Writer`, `time.Time`, `types.Importer`), i.e. source text on a label whose whole contract is naming — the same class R10 was built for, and the same spelling question this round answered for struct/interface embedding's `extends` target (`io.Reader` -> `Reader`). Both surfaces now publish the LEAF the lane would declare for the type with the package-qualified form in `metadata.qualifiedType`, matching `uses`, which had always targeted selector leaves (`pkg.Fn` -> `Fn`); the lane's own `uses`/`references` asymmetry is gone. (2) The IMPORT PATH was never a spelling at all: a module specifier is a string literal naming a module, and it rode the `references` label only because the lane published its dependency edge there (with `isImport`+`isGoImportDep` markers). That surface moved to the family's first-class `imports` label — the direction #910 took for c, and go's own requiredKinds has named `imports` since the systems wave (completeness section B pins the kind from the marker, which is unchanged). MEASURED, full draw (`bun script/m60/target-spelling-census.ts --lane go --sample 2200`: go-tools 1931 + terraform 1320): separator targets 39,280 -> 11,933, `extends|.` retired, and every remaining separator sits on an `imports` edge; probes `script/m14/tmp/go-799-reftargets.ts` (references targets carrying a separator: 1,162 `declared_type` + 56 `return_type` before, 0 after) and `go-799-hyphen-targets.ts` (the hyphen belonged to module paths — `github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp` — in files the grammar parses cleanly, so it was never debris). The residue is the module-path vocabulary the family carries as owed in 17 other lanes (`c` records exactly these three triples, `imports|.`/`imports|/`/`imports|-`, as owed): a new spelling on the REFERENCES surface now fails G1 immediately instead of hiding behind a convention recorded for a different label. ARTIFACT PROVENANCE: the go row of validation/m60/results/target-spelling.json was taken from a fresh canonical run this round (`bun script/m60/target-spelling-census.ts`, draws go-tools:40+terraform:24, syms=510 rels=2985 sep=184) and transplanted into the committed artifact, because THAT SAME full run moves NINE other lanes' rows — typescript, java, groovy, cpp, scala, kotlin, vue, zig and svelte all measure a wider separator vocabulary than their recorded rows, and java's verdict moves from `clean` to `unruled-separators`. A family-wide re-pin is those lanes' to make: the drift is real and now measured, but committing it here would have re-pinned nine lanes from a go round, and R10 live refuses any lane whose register and artifact disagree — so the alternative was a silently stale gate for all of them. The go row alone is refreshed.

DECLARED CONVENTION, from the lane's own code (src/ast/real-php-analyzer.ts resolveOverrides): every php override edge keys BOTH ends as a fully-qualified member — source `${owner}.${method}`, target `${base}.${method}` — so `.` is the lane's member qualifier, not a fabricated name, in both the verified (0.95) and the pass-3 first-parent-guess (0.5) arms. Scoped to `overrides` deliberately: a `.` in a `uses`, `calls` or `references` target is NOT covered and still fails.
RULED 2026-09-23 (R10 sibling sweep), from measurement rather than taste. The triple exists on ONE edge set only: php's include/require `references` edges, whose target is a file PATH, not a symbol name — `phpStaticIncludePath` composes the operands' values, so `require_once __DIR__ . '/bootstrap/app.php';` publishes `__DIR__/bootstrap/app.php`. Measured over 300 files of the 4,096-file php corpus set: 409 `references` edges, and the only targets carrying a dot are the 4 include paths — every one of which also carries a slash — so `references|.` and `references|/` are the SAME edge set, and no `references` target outside a path carries a dot at all. The census's own doctrine already carves this out for `imports` ("a module path is a path, not a name", recorded for svelte's route groups); php names namespaces with a backslash, which is IN this lane's alphabet, so a dot here can only be a path.

php.note: R10's first pass found two live php defects, both now fixed (#835): an include path reconstructed from a concatenation with a runtime operand (`$this->baseDir.'revision-info.php'`, phpmyadmin src/Git.php:551) and a VALUE callee published as a callee NAME (`calls -> $controller`). Both were emitted IDENTICALLY by the differential oracle because its truth came from the same rules, so no per-edge gate could see either. After the fix this lane reads clean: 0 convictions, and the only separator left is the ruled `overrides|.` convention. R10 FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-23): the third triple, `references|'`, was NOT ruled and is gone from the measurement — it was a real fabrication of the same class as the include-path fix but at the STATIC end: the rule decided a fully static concatenation was a path (correct) and then published the source text of the concatenation, so `require __DIR__ . '/src/DeprecatedClass.php'` (phpunit tests/end-to-end/regression/6778/bootstrap.php) emitted `references -> __DIR__.'/src/DeprecatedClass.php'` — quotes and operator in a target, on both sides, invisible to every per-edge gate because the oracle calls the same function. Fixed by composing operand VALUES (`__DIR__/src/DeprecatedClass.php`); the fixture php/include-paths had pinned the old spelling as correct and was re-pinned with the reason recorded, plus a reverting mutant (`php/static-concat-as-source-text`, CAUGHT). Same-file-set differential before/after on 300 phpunit files: hash 6038d82a6947594e, 4,296 truth / 4,551 analyzer edges, 0 MISSING / 0 unexplained in BOTH states — the labels moved on both sides together, which is exactly why the census is the instrument that sees it.
